title: Brazil: a census postponement is a plan change
summary: An archived IBGE English homepage records an announcement dated 17 March 2020 that moves the planned 2020 census to 2021. This case records that contemporary plan change, not the eventual completion year.
facts: Announcement label: 17 March 2020 | Archived homepage: 30 March 2020 | Plan change: 2020 → 2021
notes: Evidence is extracted text of the archived official homepage, not the full announcement or original HTML bytes. The announcement page returned 403 during the underlying review. Reasons, budgets and eventual implementation are outside this claim.

title: Japan: survey forms can affect year-on-year comparability
summary: Japan’s Statistics Bureau explains on 9 March 2018 that half the household sample began using new diary forms in January. It warns of possible discontinuity in year-on-year changes and contributions, supplies a propensity-score/inverse-probability adjustment, and records a retrospective recalculation on 8 February 2019.
facts: Survey: Family Income and Expenditure Survey | New form use: Half the sample from January 2018 | Recalculation notice: 8 February 2019
notes: The case confirms the official warning and adjustment arrangement. It does not audit every historical table or establish that every level series lacks back-calculation.

title: Greece: a flash estimate is suspended while a later release stays scheduled
summary: On 4 August 2017, ELSTAT suspends the GDP flash estimate normally released 45 days after a quarter. The planned 14 August Q2 flash estimate is cancelled, while the same notice keeps provisional Q2 data scheduled for 1 September.
facts: Notice date: 4 August 2017 | Cancelled scheduled release: 14 August 2017, Q2 flash estimate | Retained schedule: 1 September 2017, provisional Q2 data
notes: The notice establishes a suspension and a retained schedule. This case does not separately verify the September release, the duration of suspension, or motives.

title: South Africa: resumed publication retains a documented gap
summary: Stats SA states that monthly insolvency statistics resumed on 21 July 2026 with June data and a series starting in January 2023. The article identifies a September 2021–December 2022 gap and says the new release is not a continuous extension of the old series. Company liquidation statistics had continued.
facts: First resumed release reported: 21 July 2026; June reference period | Resumed series begins: January 2023 | Documented gap: September 2021–December 2022
notes: This relies on the official explanatory article; the attempted release-PDF URL returned short HTML. The gap is not by itself proof of a specific methodology change. Exact earlier suspension timing and subsequent releases are not confirmed here.

title: China: six reports keep reference quarters and page dates separate
summary: Six People’s Bank of China pages for the urban depositor, entrepreneur and banker surveys cover Q3 and Q4 2023 and display 22 March 2024 as their publication date. An official-list snapshot from 9 July 2024 contains all six links. The inherited ledger groups the three series under one delayed-publication context.
facts: Reports: 3 surveys × 2 quarters = 6 | Reference periods: 2023 Q3 and Q4 | Displayed publication date: 22 March 2024 | Historical visibility confirmed by: 9 July 2024 list snapshot
notes: The page date does not establish first public availability that day. An expected October date was only an inherited cadence estimate, so no exact delay length or interruption start is claimed.

title: China: receivables labels mark two definition changes
summary: The NBS industrial-profit release of 27 March 2019 replaces monthly accounts receivable with notes and accounts receivable. The 27 March 2020 release changes back to accounts receivable. Both explain the adjustments in relation to corporate financial-statement formats.
facts: 2019 publication: Notes and accounts receivable | 2020 publication: Accounts receivable | Ledger treatment: Two separate definition-change events
notes: Release months are not statistical reference periods or proven first-access times. The case does not validate all historical values, back series or publication channels. Similar labels alone do not establish comparability.

title: China: a breakdown is removed while aggregate industrial statistics continue
summary: NBS releases of 14 and 27 March 2019 explicitly remove the collective-enterprise breakdown from 2019 onward. Those releases still publish their respective aggregate industrial output and profit results.
facts: Removed detail: Collective-enterprise registration category | First reviewed releases: 14 and 27 March 2019 | Scope: One breakdown across two releases
notes: The source explanation refers to the declining weight of that registration type. This does not establish other motives or absence of related statistics from every other channel.

title: Vietnam: October CPI is a new reference month
summary: Two official releases report national October 2026 CPI inflation of 5.09% year on year. The same publications separately report 0.20% month on month and a 4.57% ten-month average. September’s 5.08% belongs to another reference month; the October value is not a revision to it.
facts: Selected measure: National all-items CPI, year on year | October 2026: 5.09% | September 2026: 5.08% | Observed at: 3 November 2026, 02:58:04 UTC
notes: The publisher displays 3 November 2026 without a clock time. Capture time proves observation, not first public availability. The date-only calendar does not support an intraday delay verdict; national, regional, monthly and cumulative measures remain separate.
